artifact.storage.statement: Local filesystem artifact storage is for development only. Live deployments must store diffs and other durable analysis artifacts in remote private object storage, while PostgreSQL stores metadata, storage keys, checksums, sizes, and references; local and remote backends should share one storage interface.

evidence.note: Production requirement established after identifying that instance-local files are ephemeral and service-bound.

aws.resource-scope.statement: Limit AWS resource reads and changes for PRism to resources identified as belonging to this project. Do not modify unrelated or shared account resources.

evidence.note: Developer explicitly authorized AWS Agent Toolkit setup under profile prism with the boundary that cloud-service changes remain within PRism project scope.

aws.s3.artifact-bucket.statement: PRism artifact storage is provisioned in ap-south-1 by CloudFormation stack prism-artifact-storage. Bucket prism-artifact-storage-prismartifactbucket-ubri8x7giofh is private, blocks public access, uses BucketOwnerEnforced and SSE-S3, has versioning enabled and an HTTPS-only bucket policy; backend IAM role and application configuration are still pending.

evidence.note: Verified the deployed stack and bucket configuration after creation. This operation created only PRism's S3 bucket and bucket policy; it did not create EC2 or RDS resources.

bob.codex.workflow.statement: Use Bob IDE as the visible primary build environment for hackathon evidence: the developer drives Bob Agent/Plan modes, skills, and parallel subtasks. Codex serves as the technical driver for project architecture and implementation, with Bob as the build-time passenger/partner; work should be coordinated through shared repo files and bounded tasks, never duplicated edits.

bob.sessions.deliverable.statement: A bob_sessions/ folder at repo root is a required hackathon deliverable. Every Bob IDE task session summary screenshot must be saved there as PNG, named clearly e.g. prism_task01_db_skeleton_summary.png. One screenshot per completed task.

bob.skill.review-pipeline-build.statement: A Bob skill file was drafted at .bob/skills/review-pipeline-build/SKILL.md covering pipeline constraints, build order, coordination rules, and what Bob sessions must not do at runtime.

build.sequence.statement: Build in this order: DB/API skeleton and facts engine; evidence gate; runtime agent and fixtures; frontend with streamed progress; authored sample repo and seeded PRs; benchmark scorer; product polish; README/demo support and Bob session evidence throughout.

coverage.provenance.statement: Coverage evidence must come from a real run and match the analyzed PR head SHA. A CI artifact is acceptable only when its workflow run is tied to that exact head SHA; otherwise run tests in an isolated environment for the authored sample repo or report coverage as unknown and emit no coverage-gap claim.

evidence.note: Bob's suggested latest Actions artifact needs exact-SHA validation.

data.provenance.statement: All sample code, specs, and seeded PRs must be authored for this project; do not use client data, confidential or personal information, or scraped social-media data. Track public reference sources and check their commercial-use terms.

database.local.statement: As of 2026-09-25, local Homebrew PostgreSQL 18.3 runs on localhost:5432. A dedicated non-superuser prism role and prism database now exist; backend/.env (git-ignored, mode 0600) supplies the app URL, and Alembic revision 0001 has been applied.

evidence.note: Read-only inspection; no PostgreSQL settings or databases were changed.
Initialized at the developer's request; machine-wide PostgreSQL authentication settings were left unchanged.

database.migration.enum-creation.statement: The initial Alembic migration explicitly created PostgreSQL enum types, then declared same-named sa.Enum columns that created those types again, causing DuplicateObjectError during upgrade. Removed the redundant explicit type creation so table column declarations create the enums once.

evidence.note: Fixed while provisioning the local PRism schema; alembic upgrade head then completed successfully.

deployment.architecture.statement: Deploy the Next.js frontend on Vercel and the FastAPI backend on AWS EC2. Use a private S3 bucket for durable PR artifacts and hosted PostgreSQL (RDS is the recommended managed option); the browser connects to the API over HTTPS for REST/SSE, and AWS secrets/roles remain server-side. Exact database service and network/domain details are still to be configured.

evidence.note: Developer selected this cloud split; local filesystem artifacts remain development-only.

evidence.gate.contract.statement: The evidence gate accepts typed findings with an explicit claim type and citations, validates every citation against PRFacts, and marks a finding verified only when every citation matches the claim contract. Unsupported findings remain available in the unverified appendix; coverage-gap claims require a specific uncovered line, while unknown-coverage claims require a file-level unknown status citation.

evidence.note: Implemented deterministic pure-Python gate interfaces and validation.

facts.coverage.stub.statement: Coverage status is always CoverageStatus.unknown in this milestone. coverage_facts.build_coverage_facts() raises NotImplementedError if a non-None artifact is passed. A future milestone will parse Cobertura XML from a CI run verified against the PR head SHA (see coverage.provenance constraint).

facts.engine.design.statement: Facts engine implemented in backend/app/facts/ as four modules: models.py (immutable frozen dataclasses), diff_facts.py (line-number extraction from PRBundle), python_deps.py (stdlib AST import walker), coverage_facts.py (always-unknown stub). compute_facts() is the sole public entry point. No LLM calls; no filesystem access by default. Python source must be passed via file_source_map; absent files produce no edges.

github.auth.statement: For an actual user-facing GitHub connection, prefer a GitHub App installation with minimum read-only permissions (Pull requests and Contents; Actions only if reading CI artifacts). A server GITHUB_TOKEN can support a controlled demo but is not equivalent to connecting each user's GitHub account.

evidence.note: Refined after reviewing Bob's ingestion proposal and current GitHub App documentation.

llm.provider.statement: Primary LLM provider is ZAI/GLM (developer has API key). If ZAI does not support the required streaming/tool-call interface, fall back to Gemini. The thin provider adapter must be written so swapping providers requires changing only the adapter class, not the agent logic.

pr.ingestion.statement: Hybrid ingestion confirmed by developer: accept either a GitHub PR URL (fetched via GitHub REST API with GITHUB_TOKEN) or a raw diff upload. Both paths normalise into a PRBundle struct. PR description/body is the spec for intent-vs-spec facet. Facts engine only consumes PRBundle.

evidence.note: Refined after reviewing Bob's ingestion proposal.

pr.spec.source.statement: Use the PR body as the default spec input for a fast workflow, while normalizing it into an explicit spec_text field and allowing a user-provided spec to supplement or override it. Author detailed PR bodies for seeded demo cases.

evidence.note: Recommended to preserve the brief's spec comparison while supporting real PR workflows.

product.scope.statement: The product is a routed, database-backed multi-page website with dashboard, PR brief and evidence, benchmark impact view, live streamed new-analysis progress, and About/How it works pages. It is not an AI-only review bot or a single-page mockup.

project.identity.statement: PRism is a hackathon product for evidence-backed code review of large or AI-generated pull requests. It aims to reduce review time and missed regressions by checking a PR against its spec, cross-file dependencies, and actual test coverage.

review.pipeline.statement: PRism uses a deterministic facts engine before any LLM reasoning, then four parallel review facets, a deterministic evidence gate, and a risk-ordered reviewer brief. Exact diff lines, coverage, and dependency edges must come from executable code rather than LLM guesses.

runtime.agent.statement: The shipped runtime agent is a synchronous/streamed, provider-swappable API-backed agent, defaulting to OpenAI behind a thin adapter. IBM Bob IDE is a development-time tool and must not be a runtime dependency or a human approval/queue step.

runtime.review.orchestration.statement: Analysis creation schedules an in-process background orchestration that computes and stores PRFacts, runs four typed review facets concurrently through the OpenAI Responses API adapter, verifies each citation against the facts, and persists citation checks with verified/unverified findings. Provider credentials come only from OPENAI_API_KEY; OPENAI_MODEL selects the model.

evidence.note: Implemented the runtime review milestone using strict Structured Outputs and the existing ArtifactStore.

stack.confirmed.statement: Confirmed stack: FastAPI (Python) + PostgreSQL local (SQLAlchemy async + Alembic) + Next.js 14 App Router + Tailwind CSS. LLM: ZAI/GLM primary, Gemini fallback, behind a BaseProvider adapter. stack.pending is now superseded.

stack.pending.statement: The implementation stack is intentionally undecided. Before scaffolding, propose a fast 48-hour stack for backend streaming, zero-ops relational storage, and a polished web frontend, then get the developer's confirmation.

storage.artifact.statement: Diffs and large artifacts are stored outside PostgreSQL via a pluggable ArtifactStore (local filesystem for dev, S3 for production). PostgreSQL holds only metadata: diff_storage_key, diff_size_bytes, diff_sha256. The backend serves artifacts through its own /analyses/{id}/diff endpoint; the S3 bucket is never made public.

storage.async.s3.statement: boto3 is synchronous; all S3 calls from FastAPI async handlers must be dispatched via asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, ...) — not get_event_loop(), which is deprecated inside a running loop in Python 3.10+. LocalArtifactStore calls go through the same path for consistency.

storage.diff.legacy-fallback.statement: GET /analyses/{id}/diff checks diff_storage_key first (artifact store path); if NULL it falls back to the inline pr.diff column (legacy rows). If both are NULL it returns 404. This makes backward compatibility explicit and correct.

storage.iam.statement: The S3 bucket prism-artifact-storage-prismartifactbucket-ubri8x7giofh exists (ap-south-1, prism-artifact-storage stack) but no application IAM role is configured. Before any live deployment the runtime must have a bucket-scoped IAM role with s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject, s3:DeleteObject. AWS credentials must never enter source control; use the SDK default credential chain.

storage.local.path-containment.statement: The original LocalArtifactStore._path used str.startswith for containment, which incorrectly passes sibling-prefix paths (e.g. /tmp/prism passes as prefix of /tmp/prism-evil). Fixed by using Path.relative_to() which correctly rejects any path not strictly under the root.

storage.orphan.cleanup.statement: After db.commit() raises, a fresh DB connection confirms whether any PR row references the stored key before deleting. Outcomes: no row -> delete; row found -> artifact kept (commit succeeded); DB unreachable -> artifact preserved, key logged at ERROR. Never delete without DB confirmation.
